title: 1963 AHSME Problem 30
statement:
Let

\[ F=\log\frac{1+x}{1-x}. \]

Form a new function \(G\) by replacing each \(x\) in \(F\) by

\[ \frac{3x+x^3}{1+3x^2}, \]

and simplify. The simplified expression \(G\) is equal to:

solutions.text:
For \(u=\frac{3x+x^3}{1+3x^2},\) \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{1+u}{1-u} &=\frac{1+3x+3x^2+x^3} {1-3x+3x^2-x^3}\\ &=\left(\frac{1+x}{1-x}\right)^3. \end{aligned} \] Therefore \(G=\log(\frac{1+x}{1-x})^3,\) so \(G=3F.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Call the substituted fraction \(u\) and simplify \(\frac{1+u}{1-u}\)
Its numerator and denominator factor as cubes
